@Calinou I have rebased my PR properly now ^^

Thanks for testing! I hadn't considered printing BBCode to the log at all, but it does make sense since there's a lot of code around formatting it and the log is a RichTextLabel. I'll try to get everything fixed!

Ok, after a few small fixes I got highlighting in rich messages working. In this state, it just adds everything as regular text without bbcode parsing, so all tags get exposed. This could be considered a bug, but I was thinking it might be useful as well? This would allow you to filter for bbcode tags as well. Maybe I could add another toggle button to toggle this behavior? But that might clutter the search bar too much. (As you can see, I still need to fix the coloring for rich messages that do not contain the search string, but that's a separate thing.) Edit: I also added the option to enable/disable BBCode parsing. This does not mean that all tags get displayed correctly, just that they're removed from the messages, and this allows you to search for strings that would otherwise be split up by tags. Would this be a good idea to add?

I am kind of getting stuck on this color changing part. The actual color parsing is done in RichTextLabel, and there's not a good way for me to retrieve the color of the parsed text from RichTextLabel. On top of that, a message could have multiple color tags (and other text processing tags, like bold and italic tags) that the filter would all need to account for. Currently all my functions just support a single highlighted and a single darkened color. Trying to fully support darkening all color tags would significantly complicate those functions. I think the simplest, most straightforward solution is just to expose all BBCode tags like is done in the screenshots above while filtering, and coloring everything gray that does not fit the search string.

What do you think?

> I think the simplest, most straightforward solution is just to expose all BBCode tags like is done in the screenshots above while filtering, and coloring everything gray that does not fit the search string.
>
> What do you think?

This could work well when combined with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/78310 to strip BBCode from the displayed text, but I'm not sure about displaying raw BBCode like this. It can make text with complex formatting nearly unreadable.

Well there is a toggle button now that enables/disables bbcode parsing, so the user can remove bbcode tags if they're in the way. Personally I barely use bbcode in my print statements and if I do it, it's just a single image tag or color tag. I'm not sure how big of a problem bbcode tags would be for other users. I used the RichTextLabel BBCode parsing functionality for this since I have access to it. Would you prefer me pulling in your branch and using the String method?
BBCode is broken without filter: And even when filtering, the link can't be clicked.

Hi @KoBeWi, first of all thank you for testing and notifying me of this issue. Could you provide more context with your issue? I was not able to replicate it on my build. When not filtering, links and other BBCode work as expected, both using `print_rich()` and `printerr()`.

Okay, I decided to just use the background color feature instead of coloring the text. I'm not sure why I didn't start with this. I think I tried this earlier but couldn't get this to work. This is way more flexible and doesn't required manually recoloring text. Still working on fully implementing this.

> When not filtering, links and other BBCode work as expected, both using print_rich() and printerr().

Try `push_error()`.

> Still working on fully implementing this.

@mFieldHouses Bump :slightly_smiling_face: Did you make further progress on this (and test this with `push_error()`)?

No, I didn't really, but thank you for reminding me of this, I'm still interested in getting this to work. This issue is just a lot more complicated than expected, largely due to BBCode, which kind of hurt my motivation, and I'm reluctant to just make changes without proper planning and discussion with the maintainers of the files this PR has effect on. My current solutions are kind of hacky, I feel, and are probably at a high chance of getting rejected/needing a lot of changes before being considered for getting merged.

currently, my implementation just strips all bbcode when filtering. Correctly incorporating bbcode in this will be a huge task, since bbcode tags need to enclose each other and cannot be mixed like 
`[b]bold [bgcolor=RED] highlighted [/b] non-bold text[/bgcolor]`, which means [bgcolor] tags cannot be injected arbitrarily in the messages.
Using push_bgcolor also behaves in the same way. Without making any changes to bbcode parsing in RichTextLabel, correctly injecting a highlight color in bbcode-containing messages will probably require a pretty large amount of processing per message. That feels unwanted in the editor log, as the default max count is 10 thousand messages and the log already starts considerably slowing down the editor at a few thousand messages (on my machine).

To somewhat compensate, I'm thinking of adding up/down buttons to automatically scroll the log to messages containing filter matches, when non-matching lines are not hidden. That would allow you to filter without bbcode, easily find matches, and just stop filtering and interact with the bbcode as normal.

What do you think, @Calinou ?

> BBCode is broken without filter: And even when filtering, the link can't be clicked. I was not able to reproduce the issue, maybe I already fixed it accidentally. Seems like a very similar issue is also present on the stable branch which has not been caused by my PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/00932449c9f372b30301d8b5fdc1be70ec12b5c0/editor/editor_log.cpp#L451

Reading through the RichTextLabel selection highlighting code, it seems it just draws colored rectangles behind the text. I could try a similar approach for filter match highlighting? This is deeply integrated in the RichTextLabel drawing code though, I'm not sure whether I can reproduce a similar effect without adding a new class that extends RichTextLabel or changing RichTextLabel itself. I'll look into it for sure.

This could be worth trying, but keep in mind we try to [prefer local solutions](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine/guidelines/best_practices.html#prefer-local-solutions). In practice, this means we should avoid introducing new features in RichTextLabel if they are only going to be useful in the editor. Unfortunately, I can't really think of a good way to implement this in a clean way.

Putting the buttons next to the search bar could cramp that bar, especially if the user does not have much width allocated to the output log dock and if more buttons are added in the future. I tried following the UI styling for the script editor, and that also makes a bar pop up at the bottom when toggling filtering mode. Although it doesn't actually displace the code. I could look into making it not displace the log text?

Another question that I'd like raise is how I do the layout and styling for filtering. My idea was to follow the script editor filtering tab. Is that a good idea, or does it not matter? I could definitely make the filtering tab more compact by using purely icon-only buttons, as KoBeWi suggested, but it would be disjointed with the other filtering UI/UX that users are probably already familiar with.

And something else regarding that filtering UI, which is not in the scope of this PR, is that I'd expect CheckButtons to be used for the filtering options in the script filtering UI? According to their own description in the docs, they ought to be used when changes are applied immediately, and CheckBoxes, which are currently used, should be used for things like configuration panels and forms, where changes are not immediately applied, but only after "saving" or "submitting". Would it favorable to change that? I could create an issue.

I have now gotten basic highlighting functionality working by very slightly modifying RichTextLabel and creating an extending class, purely for use in the editor. It works just like selection highlighting, and it doesn't influence BBCode.

So wrapped messages just don't have highlighting after the first wrap break Does anyone have any idea what could cause this? Fixed that issue. Now I'll just be implementing up/down buttons.

@Calinou could you let me know whether this approach is alright? I have not heard from you in a while. I have discovered a pretty large technical issue in my implementation that I'll need to fix, but I'll only be taking the time to do so once I know for sure that my approach is allowed.

I have added some callbacks (or whatever the correct technical term for what I did is) to RichTextLabel that are left empty in RichTextLabel, and implemented in my custom class extending RichTextLabel. I have also changed the access specificiers of one or two declarations in the header file to make my change work. This adds a minimal amount of extra lines but still gives me full access to the inner workings on RichTextLabel, which is absolutely needed to get this to work.
I don't know for sure if this is the correct approach. @bruvzg Any feedback?
